Date of birth after 31 December 1991
Detailed research plan with timeline specifying key milestones and activities
Letter of support from Swiss academic supervisor required (including short CV)
If already in Switzerland: date of entry must not be earlier than 1 August 2026

benefits: One-year Half-Fare Travelcard for Swiss public transport

requirements: Complete CV including educational background, degrees, awards, positions, publications, teaching and practical experience
Letter of motivation (max. 2 pages): reasons for stay in Switzerland, significance for future career
Research proposal on FCS/ESKAS form (max. 5 pages including summary for non-specialists)
Letter of support from an academic supervisor at a Swiss higher education institution
Short CV (max. 2 pages) from the academic supervisor
Two professors' email addresses (for recommendation letters submitted via system)

Copy of passport (dual citizens submit both)

scholarships.deadline: No single calendar deadline is published. scholarships.deadline_display: No single calendar deadline is published. Intake Open Date is specific to each individual university; please contact your university of choice for deadline information." At the University of Calgary, "The Graduate Award Competition opens November 1 of each year" and "Deadlines vary by program"; the Faculty of Graduate Studies reference deadline is February 1.
eligibility: Be a Canadian citizen, a permanent resident of Canada, or an international student.

Be enrolled as a full-time graduate student conducting full-time research at one of the participating institutions: Athabasca University, Concordia University of Edmonton, the University of Alberta, the University of Calgary or the University of Lethbridge.
Be conducting research in a key emerging technology area of information and communications technologies (ICT) or advanced materials and manufacturing technologies (AMM).

Be able to clearly articulate how your research aligns with Alberta Innovates' Applied Digital & Emerging Technology Areas and how your research can produce potential environmental, health, economic, social and other impacts for Alberta.
At the University of Calgary: be applying to, or enrolled in, a thesis-based graduate degree programme.
At the University of Calgary: have submitted your admissions application and received your University of Calgary student number (UCID).
Meet the eligibility requirements in the terms of reference of the award at the time the award is paid, even if you did not meet them at the time you applied.
requirements: Check with your institution's faculty of graduate studies for full descriptions and application details.
Submit your application to your institution; the applicant does not apply directly to Alberta Innovates.
At the University of Calgary: submit your admissions application and obtain your UCID before applying for the award.

At the University of Calgary: go to your Student Centre and click the link Apply for Graduate Funding in the Financial Aid section of your home screen, then select the Graduate Award Competition Application.
Only one application is required regardless of the number of awards you are applying for.
You may create one application per competition each year; if an application is incorrectly cancelled you must contact your graduate program to request reactivation.
Request and track your references before finalizing your application so they arrive before or by the application deadline.
New students can use their references from their admission application toward their scholarship application.

Reference letters used for admission may be used toward the scholarship competition as long as they were written within the eleven months prior to the Faculty of Graduate Studies' February 1 deadline.
Transcripts will be uploaded to the application by your program; scholarship requirements may differ from admission requirements.
Awards are based on merit; read and understand the terms of reference.
scholarships.duration: Terms vary from one to four years, depending on the recipient's time in the program. At the University of Calgary the published terms are $26,000 for master's students for up to two years and $31,000 for doctoral students for up to four years.
scholarships.application_period: Continuous at the funder level, with a seasonal intake at each institution. Alberta Innovates publishes the due date as "Continuous". At the University of Calgary the Graduate Award Competition opens November 1 each year, program deadlines vary and must be confirmed with Graduate Program Staff, and results for the Alberta Innovates competition are announced September to December. Awards are paid in the following academic year, with the majority starting in September.
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection is institution-specific. Each of the participating Alberta institutions has its own scholarship application and evaluation processes for students in full-time programmes, and Alberta Innovates directs students to their faculty of graduate studies for that information. At the University of Calgary the competition is merit-based and the applicant must be able to clearly articulate alignment with Alberta Innovates' Applied Digital & Emerging Technology Areas and the potential impacts of the work for Alberta. For the Killam and Open Doctoral categories a first-class average is required, which at the University of Calgary is a grade point average of 3.5 or higher in the last two years of study, though that published indicator is stated for those categories rather than for the Alberta Innovates category. Successful students may normally hold one GAC scholarship per year across the Open Doctoral and Special Awards categories and will be awarded the highest-value scholarship for which they are eligible.

scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are first subject to an eligibility and compliance review conducted by the AEF Programme to verify applicant eligibility and ensure all required materials have been provided; only applications meeting all requirements are advanced for merit-based evaluation. Merit review is a thorough, consistent and objective examination by evaluators who must be independent of the applicants and of the sponsoring agencies, applying pre-established criteria in four areas: the applicant's teaching experience, professional accomplishments, demonstrated leadership qualities, and interests as they relate to participating in the AEF Programme. Sponsoring federal agencies then review the highly reviewed applications on overall professional experience and demonstrated leadership qualities, the applicant's interest in and preparedness for the fellowship, alignment of the applicant's experience and subject matter expertise with the interests of the host office, and quality of recommendations, and select the top candidates as semi-finalists to interview in Washington, DC. Semi-finalists are invited to Washington, DC for three days of individual interviews and information sessions. Following interviews, final selections are made at the discretion of the sponsoring federal agencies; finalists are contacted by ORISE regarding offers. DOE selects the finalists for Congressional office placements. Recruitment and selection is done without regard to race, gender, age, colour, religion, national origin, mental or physical disability, or status as a veteran.

eligibility: Applicants must be U.S. Citizens or Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR) at the time of application and be at least 18 years of age at the time of applying.
Applicants must be enrolled full-time in a Qualified Graduate Program with the Ph.D. as their degree objective.
At the time of application, applicants must have obtained the Ph.D. candidacy at their home institution, and must have established a defined graduate thesis project and graduate thesis advisor.
The applicant's primary graduate thesis advisor must provide a Letter of Support.

Applicants must be pursuing a Ph.D. in physics, chemistry, material sciences, biology (non-medical), mathematics, engineering, computer or computational sciences, or select areas of environmental sciences at an accredited college or university in the United States or its territories.
The Ph.D. degree program pursued must require a research thesis/dissertation, with an emphasis on fundamental experimental or theoretical research.

Applicants must demonstrate that their graduate thesis research is in an area of fundamental research aligned with the DOE Office of Science Priority Research Areas identified for the 2026 SCGSR Solicitation 2.
The applicant and their primary graduate thesis advisor are responsible for identifying a collaborating research scientist at a DOE laboratory and jointly developing the research proposal.
Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientists may be from any of the participating DOE national laboratories/facilities.
The duration of the proposed research to be conducted at the DOE laboratory/facility may range from 3 to 12 consecutive months.
For applications in BES priority research areas, eligibility depends also on proximity between the applicant's university and the host DOE national laboratory.
Applicants must remain enrolled as a full-time graduate student in a qualified graduate program during the duration of the proposed SCGSR research project period at the host DOE laboratory/facility.

due dates and times
requirements: All applications must be completed through the online application system; only complete applications submitted by the deadline will be considered for review.
Materials uploaded into the online application system provide the sole basis for evaluation.

Complete all required fields: Contact Information; Academic Information including Current Graduate Program Information; Citizenship or Permanent Residency Status; Professional Information such as Scientific Publications and Awards; Graduate Thesis Advisor and Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientist Contact Information.

Submit the SCGSR research proposal, co-developed by the applicant and the collaborating DOE laboratory research scientist in consultation with the primary graduate thesis advisor, as a PDF through the online application.
Upload a PDF copy of current official graduate transcripts.
Provide official proof of Ph.D. candidacy as an official, signed letter from the Registrar's office or from the Chair, Head or Director of Graduate Studies of the applicant's academic department.
Submit two Letters of Support, one from the primary graduate thesis advisor and one from the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist, both completed through the online application system.
Indicate in the online application system which Office of Science priority research area the proposed project aligns with.
List citations of publications and awards, no more than 3 for each, in the appropriate section of the online application; do not submit supplemental materials.

The research proposal must address the stated aims in at least one of the SCGSR Priority Research Areas and must identify how the proposed research will take advantage of the DOE laboratory/facility's research capabilities and assets.

The proposed research must be an integral part of the applicant's overall doctoral thesis project and must be approved by the primary graduate thesis advisor, whose approval is made through the thesis advisor's Letter of Support.
Create an account on the SCGSR online application system well before the deadline and become familiar with the application information requested.
scholarships.duration: 3 to 12 consecutive months of research at a DOE laboratory/facility, within a project period bounded by published earliest and latest start dates
scholarships.application_period: 2026 Solicitation 2: online application opened August 12, 2026 and closes 5:00 PM ET on November 4, 2026. Offer notifications April 1 - 16, 2027. Proposed project periods may start as early as June 7, 2027 and must start no later than October 4, 2027. 2027 Solicitation 1 (tentative): application opens February 2027, applications due May 2027, offers September 2027, project periods starting November 2027 and ending no later than March 2028.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are first subject to an eligibility and compliance review. All eligible and compliant applications are then reviewed externally by subject matter experts in the field of the proposed research, using the DOE Office of Science's standard merit review processes. Two merit review criteria apply: (1) Scientific and/or Technical Merit of the Proposed Research, asking whether the research is well-conceived with a clear understanding of the scientific and technical challenges, whether the method and approach are appropriate, whether the graduate student is sufficiently well prepared, and whether DOE laboratory resources are adequate, including whether necessary access to a scientific user facility has been secured by the collaborating scientist; and (2) Relevance of the Proposed Research to Graduate Thesis Research and Training, asking whether the proposed research can make a significant contribution to the applicant's thesis project and whether it will enhance the applicant's graduate training and research skills. Applications are selected for award based on the results of peer review and other program policy factors, including availability of funds and balance of portfolio. The application materials received, including the research proposal, provide the sole basis for evaluation. Participation in other DOE programmes is collected for internal purposes only and does not affect selection.

scholarships.duration: Diploma up to three years, Bachelor's up to four years, MPhil up to two years plus six months for thesis defence, MPhil/PhD up to three years plus six months for the transfer report plus one year plus six months for the thesis defence, PhD up to three years plus six months

scholarships.selection_notes: Selection is on merit, after all attached conditions are satisfied and the host institution confirms a seat has been offered. Applicants must check their own country operation's call.
eligibility: UNHCR Tertiary Refugee Scholarship Programme (DAFI) offers qualified refugee and returnee (in selected countries*) students the possibility to earn an undergraduate degree in their country of asylum or home country

The applicant must be a recognized refugee or, where the country operation accepts them, an asylum seeker living in the country of asylum (published Rwanda wording: 'The applicant must be a recognized refugee or asylum seeker living in Rwanda')

Applicant should have been accepted to a university in the country of asylum; proof of admission must be submitted (published Rwanda wording: 'Applicant should have been accepted to a university in Rwanda. (You will have to submit proof of admission to a university.)')
Priority will be given to those who achieved excellent academic performance (published Rwanda wording)
Only one family member can apply/obtain DAFI scholarship to ensure that benefits allocated are equally given to other refugee students (published Rwanda wording)
Secondary selection criteria: female applicants and persons with special needs education are highly encouraged to apply (published Rwanda wording)
The DAFI Programme aims to provide equal opportunities for women and men (published Tajikistan wording)
requirements: Apply through the DAFI Programme Management Platform at https://unhcr-dafi-tertiary.scholarshipsplatform.com/ - the platform instructs applicants to register an account, start the application (saved in-progress) and submit it for review
DAFI Scholarship programme application is free of charge

The final status of the application is notified by email from the DAFI platform (published Azerbaijan instructions wording: 'Submit your application for review and wait for notification from UNHCR about the final status of your application. The notification should come to your e-mail address from the DAFI platform.')
For any questions about the application process, contact the country office by email using the published country list, or your nearest UNHCR office or DAFI partner
scholarships.duration: Duration follows the degree programme enrolled in: ISCED 6 bachelor's or equivalent, or ISCED 5 short-cycle tertiary / TVET of two years or more
scholarships.application_period: Country-specific. The 2026/2027 cycle ran on country-published windows in July-August 2026 (Rwanda 15 July-7 August 2026; Kyrgyzstan 7 July-21 August 2026; Slovakia 1 July-31 August 2026). New country calls for the next cycle are announced on the relevant UNHCR country help page and applications are submitted through the DAFI Programme Management Platform.
scholarships.selection_notes: The published Rwanda call states that priority will be given to applicants who achieved excellent academic performance, that only one family member may hold a DAFI scholarship, and that female applicants and persons with special needs education are highly encouraged to apply. It also states that only qualified candidates duly registered with UNHCR are invited to interviews, that names of shortlisted candidates are posted at the respective offices, and that academic documents are verified with the relevant authorities (the last two statements are published in the Windle International Kenya DAFI scholarship instructions, not on the UNHCR Rwanda call). The UNHCR programme page states that UNHCR and its education partners closely monitor scholars' academic progress and well-being through regular engagement with students and their institutions.

scholarships.selection_notes:
Aalto University Excellence Scholarships are merit-based and are granted on a competitive basis to the highest-achieving applicants based on the programme's evaluation criteria.
Each study option evaluates and ranks applications that are complete and meet the general eligibility criteria, based on its own selection criteria, which may include the relevance of previous studies, academic performance, motivation and, in the fields of art, design and architecture, a portfolio.
The applications are compared to each other, and the highest-ranked applicants are admitted; since the number of study places is restricted, not all eligible applicants will receive an offer of admission, and study options are not required to fill all available places.
There is a very limited number of scholarships available, and programmes may also decide not to grant any scholarships.
For the bachelor's-to-master's continuation route: completion of the bachelor's degree within the target time period and a weighted average grade of at least 3.50, calculated from the completed degree in its entirety.

eligibility: The applicant must be an Indian citizen currently residing in India.

The applicant must be a graduate (hold a Bachelor's degree) from a recognised institute/university in India.
In the absence of a Bachelor's degree, they must carry at least three years of relevant work experience.
Those enrolled in academic studies/PhD for the duration of the fellowship are NOT eligible to apply.

requirements: Complete all questions in the Foundation's Online Application System (OAS)
Enter name, address and latest contact information correctly
For the 'Topic of your project' field, describe the fellowship activity in a few lines so that it correctly represents the nature of the project
Statement of purpose and work plan must be completed in the Foundation's own format and uploaded as PDF only
Your Statement of purpose and work plan must not exceed 1000 words each
The statement of purpose must outline the applicant's personal and professional trajectory very briefly, and the motivation for taking up the project and how it contributes to social change

The work plan must include a title of the proposed work with a concise description of the work or research planned during the fellowship, the expected outcomes, and in detail the manner in which the project will be undertaken with a clear timeline for 2 years
Two letters are required: a Mentor endorsement letter and a Recommendation letter

The Mentor endorsement letter must include a brief description of the mentor's work experience, the mentor's contact details (email and official address), a statement of why the mentor endorses the applicant's work plan, a statement that the mentor agrees to supervise the applicant's work during the fellowship, willingness to review and comment on quarterly and annual progress reports, and willingness to hold periodic meetings with the Foundation so it can assess the fellow's progress

The Letter of Recommendation must elaborate the nature of engagement with the applicant (in what capacity they engaged with the applicant) and the reason why the referee would like to recommend the applicant and the work plan

The Recommendation letter must be from a person who has supervised the applicant's work for at least 6 months; this cannot be the same person as the mentor. For fresh graduates, an academic letter of recommendation is acceptable
The mentor or referee cannot be someone who is currently an Inlaks Fellow or currently being supported by Inlaks under any other opportunity
Please ensure that both the Mentor and Referee letters are also submitted by 15th November 2026, 11:59pm

eligibility: Candidate eligibility (both conditions must be satisfied at the time of application, at the time of selection, and during the fellowship period): (1) Be a citizen or permanent resident of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan. (Taiwan and Palestine are treated in this manner.) Persons of Japanese nationality are eligible to apply if they have resided at the time of application in a foreign country for 10 years or longer and are judged at a host research institution to have played an active role in that country's scientific community. (2) Be a full-time researcher or person with full-time researcher status at a university or research institution in a foreign country and have a position equivalent to a professor, associate professor or assistant professor in Japan (including positions such as professor emeritus). Researchers of other status may apply if it has been six years or longer since they obtained their doctoral degree and the host research institution judges them to have continuously conducted research at a foreign university or research institution.

Host researcher (applicant) eligibility: be affiliated with a research institution specified in Article 2 of the Procedure for the Handling of Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research (KAKENHI) issued by MEXT, be eligible to apply for a KAKENHI grant, and wish to host an overseas researcher.

Host researcher eligibility: be a full-time researcher. However, researchers who are not employed full time may be eligible if the host institution judges them able to execute their responsibility to carrying out the program uninterruptedly throughout the Fellow's tenure including providing them a suitable research environment (e.g. laboratory, space, facilities and personnel) in the same way that a full-time researcher would be able to do.
Selection policy requires that the applicant (host researcher) and candidate have established contact in advance and created a concrete activity plan.
requirements: Applications must be submitted to JSPS by a host researcher in Japan via the head of their university or institution.

scholarships.duration: 14 to 60 days
scholarships.application_period: FY2027 2nd recruitment: host-institution submissions to JSPS by 5 p.m. JST on 23 April 2027; selection results published in early August 2027; periods for arrival in Japan 1 October 2027 - 31 March 2028. The JSPS Electronic Application System becomes available approximately two months before each JSPS deadline.
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection of the applicant (host researcher) and the candidate (invited overseas researcher) is done by the JSPS International Program Committee, made up of Japan's frontline researchers. Selection is carried out through a document review in the first stage and a panel review in the second. Reviewers with a potential conflict of interest are removed, and all Review Committee Members must comply with confidentiality and non-disclosure agreements. Document reviews are conducted by three examiners per application, using a graduated 1-5 scale (5 superlative, 4 excellent, 3 good, 2 fair, 1 poor), taking into account research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity and future potential; the averaged document-review score is the primary screening criterion for panel review. Two selection judgements are made: Selected and Not-selected.

eligibility: Research students: You must be under 35 years of age and be eligible for admission to a master's program or a doctoral program (first or second stage) at a Japanese graduate school.

requirements: Application must be made through a Japanese embassy or consulate general in the applicant's own country (Embassy Recommendation route).

scholarships.selection_notes: Applicants are recruited and initially screened by the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their country, which sits its own qualifying examinations (Japanese and English for research students), conducts the interview and collects all required documents; MEXT then selects the scholarship students and allocates them to host graduate schools, subject to the host university's acceptance.

scholarships.title: NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program (NSF GRFP)
scholarships.deadline: Annual NSF GRFP: Oct 2026 deadlines by field
scholarships.deadline_display: Annual NSF GRFP: Oct 2026 deadlines by field
eligibility: At the time of submission, must be a U.S. citizen, national, or a permanent resident ("green-card" holder).
Must intend to enroll or be enrolled full-time in an eligible research-based master's or doctoral degree program in an eligible field of study in STEM.
Must never have previously accepted an NSF Graduate Research Fellowship.
Must have declined any previously offered NSF Graduate Research Fellowship by the deadline (if applicable).

Must have completed less than one academic year in a graduate degree program according to the institution's academic calendar; non-degree coursework must be clearly identified in the transcript and does not count toward this limit.
Must not be a current NSF employee.

Degree programs must be at a nonprofit institution of higher education accredited in, and having a campus located in, the United States, its territories, or possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.
An eligible applicant can submit only one application per annual competition.

Fellowships may only be used for an eligible graduate degree program at a nonprofit academic institution accredited in, and having a campus located in, the U.S., its territories, possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.
requirements: Prepare and submit the application in the GRFP Application Module on Research.gov.
Create a Research.gov account to access the module.
Provide accurate personal information: full legal name, mailing address, permanent address, date of birth, high school location, and demographic information.
Select a level (Level 1 undergraduate, or Level 2 graduate) in the application.
Provide the list of institutions, enrollment status, enrollment dates and degree conferred (if applicable) for all degree-granting undergraduate and graduate institutions attended.
Provide significant academic honors, fellowships, scholarships, publications and presentations.
Select the Major Field of Study most closely aligned with the proposed graduate program and research plan; the Major Field of Study determines the application deadline and the reviewers.

Request reference letters in the GRFP Application Module and rank them in order of preference; three reference writer names and contact information are required, and two reference letters must be received by NSF.
Provide a Personal, Relevant Background, and Future Goals Statement of a maximum of three pages with headings for Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts.
Provide a Graduate Research Plan Statement of a maximum of two pages with headings for Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts.
Reference letters are due before the NSF GRFP application deadlines, by 8:00 p.m. Eastern time on the reference letter date in the Notice of Funding Opportunity.
All materials are submitted through the GRFP Application Module; emailed and/or physically mailed applications will not be accepted.
Applications are automatically checked by the GRFP Application Module for compliance with the format requirements; documents that are not compliant will not be accepted by the module.
scholarships.duration: Five-year fellowship period with three years of financial support
scholarships.application_period: The GRFP Application Module usually opens in July or August; applications for the 2027 competition close between October 19 and October 23, 2026 depending on Major Field of Study, with reference letters due October 16, 2026. The module opened in time for the 2026 application cycle; the 2027 application deadlines were published August 25, 2026.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are reviewed by disciplinary and interdisciplinary scientists, engineers and STEM experts selected by NSF Program Officers, with care taken to ensure no conflicts of interest. Applications are reviewed in broad areas of related disciplines based on the Major Field of Study selected by the applicant, using the two NSF Merit Review Criteria: Intellectual Merit (potential to advance knowledge) and Broader Impacts (potential to benefit society and contribute to specific, desired societal outcomes). Intellectual Merit factors include the ability to plan and conduct research, work independently, work as part of a team, interpret and communicate research, take initiative, think creatively, solve problems, persist and overcome challenges, and demonstrated intellectual ability as indicated by grades, coursework and awards. Broader Impacts factors include increasing participation in STEM, improving STEM education through outreach and mentoring, increasing public scientific literacy, increasing collaboration among academia and industry, improving educator development, improving societal well-being, developing a globally competitive STEM workforce, improving national security, increasing U.S. economic competitiveness, and enhancing research and education infrastructure. GRFP was established to recruit and support individuals who demonstrate the potential to make significant contributions in STEM.

scholarships.title: Appel à projets M-ERA.NET 2026/27 - Science et ingénierie des matériaux pour l'innovation en Europe (édition 2027 pour l'ANR)
scholarships.deadline: Limite de dépôt des projets : 18/11/2026 à 12:00 CET. The two-step schedule is: "Étape 1 : 12/05/2026, 12 h 00 (CEST)" (pre-proposals, closed) and "Étape 2 : 18/11/2026, 12 h 00 (CET)" (detailed proposals). Only coordinators whose pre-proposal was recommended by at least three funding agencies from at least three different participating countries and who received the M-ERA.NET invitation may deposit a detailed proposal in step 2. Partners requesting ANR aid must additionally deposit their detailed proposal on the ANR submission site, with the exact link and deadline communicated later by email.
scholarships.deadline_display: Limite de dépôt des projets : 18/11/2026 à 12:00 CET. The two-step schedule is: "Étape 1 : 12/05/2026, 12 h 00 (CEST)" (pre-proposals, closed) and "Étape 2 : 18/11/2026, 12 h 00 (CET)" (detailed proposals). Only coordinators whose pre-proposal was recommended by at least three funding agencies from at least three different participating countries and who received the M-ERA.NET invitation may deposit a detailed proposal in step 2. Partners requesting ANR aid must additionally deposit their detailed proposal on the ANR submission site, with the exact link and deadline communicated later by email.
eligibility: The pre-proposal or proposal must correspond to one (and only one) scientific collaboration theme defined in the call.
Maximum project duration is 3 years (36 months).

Minimum consortium composition of 3 Partners requesting funding from a funding agency listed in Annex 3 of the call text and eligible for that funding, from at least three different countries, of which at least two are EU Member States or Horizon Europe associated countries participating in M-ERA.NET Call 2026. Partners not requesting funding may participate if this minimum is met.
The coordinator must request funding from one of the agencies participating in M-ERA.NET Call 2026 and be eligible there.
The involvement of a single Partner must not exceed 60% of the total involvement (measured in person-months) of the proposal.
The involvement of Partners from a single country must not exceed 70% of the total involvement (measured in person-months).

If one or more Partners are not eligible (or not invited to step 2) and their total effort is equal to or greater than 15% of the total project effort (in person-months), the entire pre-proposal or detailed proposal is discarded from the selection process.
To be invited to submit a detailed proposal in step 2, the pre-proposal must be recommended by at least three funding agencies from at least three different countries participating in the Call 2026.

A pre-proposal containing one or more Partners requesting ANR aid must clearly indicate the topic studied and the TRL levels of the tasks of each French partner in the consortium, and must be deposited on the ANR submission site in step 2, in addition to the deposit on the call site, providing all the information requested on the site.

A pre-proposal or proposal must correspond to one of the ANR-eligible topics: 1. Materials for energy storage and distribution systems; 2. Materials for energy conversion; 4. Innovative functional materials with designed architectures; 6. Next-generation materials for electronics. The relevance of the proposal to the chosen topic must be clearly justified from step 1; proposals not matching these topics are rendered ineligible for ANR funding.

The final TRL of the project must not exceed 5 for an ANR-funded partner, on pain of ineligibility, and the work carried out by partners requesting ANR aid must necessarily be positioned either in the "fundamental research" segment or in the first "applied research" segment.

Partners, legal or natural persons, subject to European Union sanctions are excluded from the call; the ANR declares ineligible any partner requesting its aid who is associated within the submitted project with partners covered by a sanction measure. As of publication this concerns in particular partners from Russia and Belarus, and partners from territories of Ukraine escaping the control of the Ukrainian government. The list is non-exhaustive and may change with new EU sanctions.

A project proposal may not be similar in whole or in part to another proposal submitted to any ANR call under evaluation (all calls and all evaluation stages) or funded by the ANR. Similarity is established when the projects describe identical main objectives or result from a simple adaptation.
A researcher may request ANR aid (whether as partner, coordinator or co-coordinator) for only one proposal in the 2026/27 M-ERA.NET call.
Each project Partner must meet its own funding agency's national or regional criteria, including its TRL requirements, and must be selected by that agency to receive funding.
requirements: Pre-proposals and detailed proposals, written in English, must be deposited by the project coordinator on the M-ERA.NET Call 2026 submission site.
Use of the templates available on the M-ERA.NET site is mandatory; any unauthorised modification, in particular exceeding the page limit, may render the proposal ineligible.
The pre-proposal must be the duly completed pre-proposal form, in English, complying with the mandatory layout conditions.

The detailed proposal must be the duly completed detailed-proposal form in English, complying with the mandatory layout conditions, and must include Annex 1 describing the Partner profiles together with the CVs of all consortium participants, also in English.

Partners requesting ANR aid invited to step 2 must additionally deposit their detailed proposal on the ANR submission site, with information identical to the central deposit; the exact link and deadline are communicated later by email.
National and regional eligibility, selection and funding rules apply at both steps, and for some countries/regions restrictions on topics, TRL levels and the type of eligible partners apply.
The scientific and technological objectives stated in the pre-proposal cannot be modified at step 2.

It is not possible to add Partners from new countries to the consortium in step 2; only new Partners from countries already involved in the pre-proposal via a funding request to one of their funding agencies may be added.

Any change must be communicated to and accepted by the requested funding agencies and the call secretariat at least two weeks before the step 2 closing date, with the consortium coordinator ensuring acceptance.

The scientific lead (Responsable scientifique) formally commits that their hierarchy (administrative and financial services and persons legally entitled to represent the managing institution, or their representatives) has approved the submission and that the information has been communicated to them.

French project leaders (requesting funding or not) ensure compliance with the national research professions deontology charter and the ANR deontology and scientific-integrity charter within the research activities carried out under their responsibility.

Where genetic resources are used, all participants (requesting funding or not) must respect the Nagoya Protocol obligations, and beneficiaries under the access-and-benefit-sharing regulation must provide the Due Diligence Declaration receipt by the date of the final payment.
Where relevant, take into account the sex and/or gender dimension in the research and give equitable visibility to the work produced.

Before any ANR project deposit, applicants should approach their institution's defence and security officer or PPST services to verify their project's eligibility conditions; projects with foreign public or private partners are subject to SHFDS/MESR opinion, and a negative opinion prevents selection.
scholarships.duration: Maximum project duration is 3 years (36 months).
scholarships.application_period: Ouverture : 31/03/2026 à 09:00 CEST. Limite de dépôt des pré-dossiers : 12/05/2026 à 12:00 CEST (step 1, closed). Limite de dépôt des projets : 18/11/2026 à 12:00 CET (step 2, open on 2026-10-01). An information webinar was held on 18 March 2026, 12:00-14:00 CET, with presentations and the recording available on the M-ERA.NET call site.
scholarships.selection_notes: Evaluation and selection are centralised at M-ERA.NET level and take place in two steps: step 1 central evaluation of pre-proposals by independent international experts convened by the M-ERA.NET Call Secretariat, with invitations to step 2 issued in ranking order and taking account of the participating agencies' budget capacity; step 2 central evaluation of detailed proposals by independent international experts convened by the same secretariat. Proposals are ranked on the evaluation results and selection follows the ranking. The list of projects recommended for funding is drawn up by the group of participating funders taking account of their respective budget capacities, and the final funding decision is then taken individually by the funders concerned. Results are sent by the call secretariat to the project coordinators. Evaluation modalities and criteria are those of the call text (Guide for proposers) available on the ANR call page and the M-ERA.NET call site; the ANR adds its own horizontal objectives, which are that projects show significant French participation (in coordination or in charge of a substantial part of the work), generate significant opening and diversification of French collaboration networks, and are ambitious with a clear intention of continuity and evolution of the collaboration. During discussions to separate projects of similar scientific quality within the funder group, projects involving a wider and/or more diverse consortium may be favoured.

scholarships.selection_notes: Only proposals satisfying the eligibility criteria (critères de recevabilité) are transmitted to the evaluation committee and can in no case be funded. Eligible projects are assessed by an independent international-dimension committee convened by the ANR, which may call on external experts and may hear project leaders (with project representatives) after sending questions in advance. The committee produces (1) a list of projects it recommends for funding on the published criteria and (2) a list it proposes not to fund because quality is insufficient on at least one criterion, with a written justification for each project, and may give an opinion on the amount requested. Uninvolved PEPR GFM programme directors then propose to the SGPI which projects could be financed and at what amount; the Prime Minister, after opinion of the CPMo and the SGPI, decides beneficiaries and amounts, and each project is covered by a contract between the ANR and the coordinating institution. Evaluation criteria fall into three groups: (a) scientific ambition and excellence (research question going beyond the documented state of the art, discipline combination justified by the question, dialogue of conceptual frameworks, ethical questions treated as integral to ambition); (b) quality of the consortium, resources mobilised and governance (recognised complementary expertise, adequacy of staff with objectives including a precise role and career benefit for each contractual worker, structured maturation phase, mechanisms for shared appropriation of questions, inventory/acquisition/management strategy for data and samples, recurrent ethical monitoring mechanisms, explicit choices to minimise the environmental footprint, coherent sizing with an argued 0.8-3 M€ budget); (c) fit with the PEPR GFM challenges and impact (clear fit with at least one challenge and the programme's strategic priorities, described scientific/economic/environmental/societal impacts, described sharing of data and results, open-access data strategy with FAIR and CARE and Opidor PGD links, dissemination to academic and non-academic audiences).

Valorise the research and innovation produced, accompanying clinical implementation and/or industrialisation.

scholarships.selection_notes: Only proposals meeting the eligibility criteria (critères de recevabilité) are transmitted to the evaluation committee and can in no case be funded. Eligible projects are evaluated by an independent international-dimension committee, which may use external experts and may hear project leaders (with project representatives) after transmitting questions in advance. The committee delivers to the PEPR PROPSY scientific directors a report with a list of projects recommended for funding, a list of projects it proposes not to fund for insufficient quality on at least one criterion, a written justification for every project, and possibly an opinion on the amounts requested. The PEPR PROPSY scientific directors then propose to the SGPI which projects could be financed and at what amount; the Prime Minister, after SGPI opinion, decides beneficiaries and amounts, and each project is covered by a contract between the ANR and the coordinating institution. Evaluation criteria fall into three groups: (1) excellence and scientific ambition in precision psychiatry - clarity of objectives and hypotheses, innovativeness, ambition, originality, methodological or conceptual rupture against the state of the art, methodological relevance, preliminary data, project feasibility; (2) quality of the consortium, project management, resources mobilised and governance - competence, expertise and involvement of the project leader including capacity to coordinate ambitious multidisciplinary projects or consortia, academic track record, international recognition, quality and complementarity of the scientific consortium, adequacy between human and financial means and the objectives, relevance of the schedule and management of scientific risks with alternative solutions and credible milestones, relevance and efficiency of governance including patient associations and links with industrial partners or other programmes; (3) impact and outcomes - capacity to address precision-psychiatry development issues, active strategy to measure economic and/or societal impact, contribution to solutions for pathophysiological, diagnostic or therapeutic issues, dissemination and valorization strategy in itinere and ex post, adherence to FAIR and Open Science principles and promotion of scientific culture. Committee members and external experts commit to ANR deontology and integrity rules, strict confidentiality, declaration of conflicts of interest, and a ban on AI tools in the evaluation.

scholarships.title: Wellcome Early-Career Award
scholarships.deadline: There are no deadlines for applications to this scheme. Applications can be submitted at any time. Apply anytime - Applications are accepted year-round.
scholarships.deadline_display: There are no deadlines for applications to this scheme. Applications can be submitted at any time. Apply anytime - Applications are accepted year-round.
eligibility: You should be able to demonstrate the ability to conduct independent, original research that makes a meaningful contribution to knowledge, achieved through completion of a PhD or equivalent higher research degree (you must have passed your thesis defence by the date you submit your application), or through at least four years' research experience equivalent to a PhD.

Any periods of research undertaken during an undergraduate or Master's degree are not counted as equivalent research experience, and you must not have started a PhD or equivalent higher research degree if relying on the experience route.

You may have some postdoctoral experience in your proposed field of study, but no more than three years at the date of submission unless you can demonstrate how other factors have impacted on your research career.

You must be able to contribute at least 80% of your research time in support of the project proposed in the award, and should not spend more than 20% of your time on non-research related activities; if you are in a clinical craft speciality you may spend up to 40% of your time on clinical duties.

If you are a health professional and want to continue with clinical activities, you must be registered with, and be licensed by, the relevant professional regulator in the country you intend to work in.

Your administering organisation must be in the UK, the Republic of Ireland, or a low- or middle-income country apart from India and mainland China; the organisation must be not-for-profit and can be a higher education institution, research institute or healthcare organisation.

Your sponsor must be an individual at your administering organisation holding an established post (or an honorary academic appointment) for the duration of the award, and must guarantee the space and resources you will need from the start date to the end date of the award.
You should also identify a mentor for the period of your award with a track record in training and mentorship; your sponsor can also be your mentor. Sponsors and mentors are not paid for their input.
Coapplicants are not accepted.
You may only have one application under consideration as a lead applicant at any one time for the Early Career Award, Career Development Award and Discovery Award schemes.

Your research must fit within what Wellcome supports in Discovery Research and have the potential to improve human life, health and wellbeing; it can be in any discipline including STEM, experimental medicine, humanities and social science, clinical/allied health sciences and public health.
requirements: Submit your application through Wellcome Funding, and only once all required sections and documents are complete
Obtain a sponsor statement from an individual at your administering organisation who holds an established post for the duration of the award
Identify a mentor with a track record in training and mentorship
If requesting overheads, provide a letter from your Finance Director stating how overhead costs were calculated, including confirmation of any externally validated rate and when it was last reviewed
You must check that your type of research project is within what Wellcome funds in Discovery Research before applying
scholarships.duration: Usually 5 years, but may be less for some disciplines, and may only be longer if held on a part-time basis
scholarships.application_period: Rolling, applications accepted year-round. Location eligibility changes on 29 October 2026: from that date applications are only accepted from lead applicants based at eligible administering organisations in the UK and low- and middle-income countries in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia. Applications submitted on or before 28 October 2026 are assessed under the current location eligibility requirements.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are assessed through Wellcome's shortlisting Advisory Groups and then peer review. The same project may be submitted for consideration a maximum of two times across all Wellcome funding schemes and themed funding calls, and resubmissions must include significant changes demonstrating clear development of the original proposal. If your application scores in the lowest levels at the shortlisting meeting you will not be permitted to resubmit. If unsuccessful with an Early-Career Award, you may submit one further application for the same project to any Wellcome scheme, provided you still meet the eligibility criteria.
scholarships.name: Wellcome Early-Career Award

The selection committee meets eight to ten times a year and decides on admission; the applicant is informed at the latest one week after the meeting. All applicants are informed by email at each stage. 'Above average' refers to the average grade in the subject at the university location or in the training occupation.

scholarships.deadline_display: "APPLICATION DEADLINE: 16:00/4:00 PM GMT on Tuesday, October 13, 2026" and "The deadline for applications for the Mandela Washington Fellowship is 16:00/4:00 PM GMT on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. Applications must be submitted using the online application system at apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org." "There is no fee to apply for the Mandela Washington Fellowship."
eligibility: Are between the ages of 25 and 35 as of the application deadline (October 13, 2026), although exceptional applicants ages 21-24 may be considered
Are not U.S. citizens or permanent residents of the United States
Are eligible to receive a United States J-1 visa
Are not employees or immediate family members (spouses, parents, children, or siblings) of employees of the U.S. Government (including a U.S. embassy or consulate or other U.S. Government entity)
Are proficient in reading, writing, and speaking English (applicants who are deaf should refer to the English Language instructions in the application instructions)

Are citizens of one of the following countries: Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Cabo Verde, Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Republic of the Congo, Cote d'Ivoire, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Eritrea, Eswatini, Ethiopia, Gabon, The Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Niger, Nigeria, Rwanda, Sao Tome and Principe, Senegal, Seychelles, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Africa, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania, Togo, Uganda, Zambia, or Zimbabwe
Are residents of one of the above countries, and will be permanently residing there as of February 1, 2027, and at the beginning of the Fellowship in June 2027
Are not alumni or prior participants of the Mandela Washington Fellowship
requirements: Applications must be submitted using the online application system at apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org; "Applications and information submitted via email or other means will not be considered."
You must complete all fields marked with a red asterisk (*).
You must answer all application questions in English, and answers must reflect your own experiences and ideas.

You do not have to finish your application in one session. You may save your work and return as many times as necessary; however "Once you have submitted your application, however, you can no longer add any additional information or make any changes."
All answers in the application, including written responses to essays and optional PDE questions, must be your own original work, based on your own creativity and effort.

Your application will be disqualified if you copy language from other Fellowship applications (including those of other applicants or Fellowship alumni) or from other sources (including websites or blogs), as this is considered plagiarism.

Responsible use of technology is permitted with transparency: "If you use any technology (including AI) to help prepare your responses, you must disclose this where asked in the application, and you remain responsible for the content you submit."

In the online application system, after fully completing a section it will be marked as "Completed." When all required sections are marked as "Completed," click "Submit Application" at the bottom of the application dashboard; your application is not complete until you submit it.
If selected as a semi-finalist, you must provide a copy of your international passport (if available) or other government-issued photo identification at the interview.
If your technical eligibility for the Fellowship changes at any point, you must email MWFellowship@irex.org, as well as your local U.S. embassy or consulate, immediately.
The Fellowship Terms and Conditions require all Fellows to attend and fully participate in all required sessions and program activities scheduled by their institute.

All individuals who are selected for the Fellowship will be required to have a passport from an eligible Fellowship country that is valid through at least February 28, 2028, or through March 31, 2028, if selected for the Professional Development Experience.
scholarships.duration: "A six-week institute program" at a U.S. college or university, "from mid-June through early August 2027", plus an optional four-week Professional Development Experience, for a total of "approximately 10 weeks" for PDE Fellows
scholarships.application_period: Application opened 22 September 2026 and closes at 16:00/4:00 PM GMT on Tuesday 13 October 2026 for the 2027 Fellowship. Semi-finalists are interviewed by U.S. embassies and consulates from October 2026 to January 2027; applicants are notified of their status in February/March 2027; visa processing and pre-Fellowship activities for finalists run from March to May 2027; the Fellowship begins in the United States in June 2027, with institutes running from mid-June through early August 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: "The Fellowship selection process is a merit-based open competition." After the deadline, all eligible applications are reviewed and scored against the published criteria: proficiency speaking, reading and writing in English; a proven record of accomplishment in business, trade, emerging technologies, governance and/or security; a demonstrated and clear interest in building and maintaining partnerships with American organizations and businesses that advance shared goals; a commitment to return to Sub-Saharan Africa and contribute skills and talents; the ability to work cooperatively in groups and to respect others; strong social and communication skills; and demonstrated adaptability and the ability to lead effectively in varying and changing environments. Applicants who do not meet the technical eligibility requirements "will not be forwarded to the selection committee." Semi-finalists are then interviewed in person by the U.S. embassy or consulate in their home country between October 2026 and January 2027. Selected finalists must participate in mandatory Pre-Fellowship Orientation activities and a visa interview within Sub-Saharan Africa. The U.S. Department of State and IREX "reserve the right to verify all information included in the application", requiring documentation of age, citizenship and residency at the interview stage; any discrepancy or false information means "the application will be immediately declared invalid and the applicant ineligible." PDE applicants are assessed separately on the ability to work professionally in a U.S. organization, articulation of clear and specific learning goals, flexibility, alignment between professional background, institute track and potential U.S. organizations, interest in sustaining engagement with U.S. professionals, and strong English proficiency.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship (U.S. Department of State educational and cultural exchange programme, administered by IREX)

scholarships.title: Flanders Trainee Programme (Flanders Traineeship Programme)
eligibility: You are younger than 35 on the start date of your internship.
You have obtained a secondary or higher education diploma in Flanders. So your nationality and official place of residence are irrelevant.
You have secured an internship with a multilateral organisation from the published qualifying list.
The internship lasts at least two and up to six months.
The internship must take place at the headquarters or a field office of the organisation, within the areas of jurisdiction of the Diplomatic Representations of Flanders.
requirements: Be under 35 on the internship start date
Hold a secondary or higher education diploma obtained at a Flemish educational institution
Have secured the internship; you may apply up to six months before it starts or after it has started
Your internship supervisor must complete the attestation regarding the internship offer and submit it to stages.dkbuza@vlaanderen.be
If you apply after the internship has started, the remaining period counted from the first day after you submit must be at least two months
After the internship, submit the personal evaluation form and have your supervisor complete and submit the evaluation form, at the latest two months after the end of the internship
Take part in an intake interview before the internship and a follow-up conversation afterwards
You must not receive a salary from the hosting organisation if you want to keep the Flemish Growth Package/child benefit
Inform the programme if you end the internship early; you may have to repay part of the grant
scholarships.duration: The grant covers an internship of at least two and up to six months. The internship can be extended to a total duration of six months, or nine months where the internship concerns a project funded by the Government of Flanders.
scholarships.application_period: The 2026 budget is exhausted and applications for 2026 are closed. The 2027 budget reopens for applications in January 2027 for internships taking place in 2027, and new internship vacancies will be published on the programme's internships page from late 2026 onwards. Inside a funded budget year the published rule is that you may apply at any time of the year until one day before your internship starts, up to six months in advance, but a grant is only granted while budget remains.
scholarships.selection_notes: No competitive jury or published ranking is described for this programme. The published route is a budget-limited reimbursement scheme: in principle you can apply at any time of the year, but you only get a grant if budget is still available, and if a budget is no longer available for the current year that is announced clearly on the programme website; an application submitted after the budget is gone is not processed and is not kept until a new budget is available. The average administrative turnaround time is three weeks. The grant is reduced by any remuneration or financial allowance you receive for the same internship from another Belgian or foreign government or from the multilateral organisation itself.
scholarships.name: Flanders Trainee Programme (Flanders Traineeship Programme)

scholarships.title: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP) 2027 - Application Window for Japanese Nationals
scholarships.deadline: The 2027 application window for Japanese nationals will open from February 15 to April 16, 2027. As from February 15, 2027, prospective candidates are invited to express their interest to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat with an email to scholarshipapplicants@worldbank.org. Winners are informed by mid-July, after the JJ/WBGSC approval. The 2026 application window for Japanese nationals closed on Friday 17 April 2026.
scholarships.deadline_display: The 2027 application window for Japanese nationals will open from February 15 to April 16, 2027. As from February 15, 2027, prospective candidates are invited to express their interest to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat with an email to scholarshipapplicants@worldbank.org. Winners are informed by mid-July, after the JJ/WBGSC approval. The 2026 application window for Japanese nationals closed on Friday 17 April 2026.
eligibility: Be a Japanese national

On or after the date the call for scholarship applications opens, not be an Executive Director, his/her alternate, and/or staff of any type of appointment (including temporary and consultant) of the World Bank Group (The World Bank, International Development Association, International Finance Corporation, Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, and International Center for Settlements of Investment Disputes), and not be a close relative of any of the aforementioned by blood or adoption (close relative defined as Mother, Father, Sister, Half-sister, Brother, Half-brother, Son, Daughter, Aunt, Uncle, Niece, or Nephew)
Hold a bachelor's degree (or equivalent university degree) earned at least three years before the date of the Application Deadline

On or after the date the JJ/WBGSP scholarship application process opens, not be employed (as a staff or any type of employment) by the Government of Japan or its related agencies, including JICA, local governments and the Central Bank

Have at least 3 years of paid development-related employment acquired since earning a bachelor's degree (or equivalent university degree) and acquired within the past six years from the date of the Application Deadline

At the time of the application submission, be either admitted unconditionally (except for financing) or currently enrolled full-time in a graduate program outside of Japan in an area of study related to development, or be currently employed full-time in development-related work pertaining directly to developing countries
requirements: Register interest with the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat by emailing scholarshipapplicants@worldbank.org from February 15, 2027
Details on eligibility criteria for each call for applications are provided in that call's Application Guidelines, and those detailed criteria are strictly adhered to with no exceptions

Be admitted unconditionally (except for financing) to, or currently enrolled full-time in, a graduate program outside of Japan in an area of study related to development, or be currently employed full-time in development-related work pertaining directly to developing countries
Inform and document to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat any other sources of scholarship funds if notified of being a semi-finalist or awarded a scholarship
scholarships.duration: Up to two years; all JJ/WBGSP scholarships cover the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less
scholarships.application_period: A single application window for the 2027 cycle for Japanese nationals, from February 15 to April 16, 2027. From the opening date, prospective candidates are invited to register interest with the Secretariat by email. Results are communicated by mid-July 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: Two qualified assessors independently review each eligible application and score it on a scale of 1 to 10 on four factors: Quality of Academic Experience and Recommendation (20% weight), Quality of Professional Recommendations (20% weight), Quality of Professional Experience (20%), and Commitment to International Development Career (40% weight). The Secretariat uses the average score of the two assessors plus maintaining a reasonable distribution of awards across gender and giving scholarships to those applicants who, other things being equal, have limited access to financial resources for graduate studies abroad. Finalists are presented to the JJ/WBG Steering Committee, composed of members of the World Bank Board of Directors and World Bank management, for approval.
scholarships.program_type: Development bank scholarship (bilateral government-funded graduate scholarship)
scholarships.name: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP) 2027 - Application Window for Japanese Nationals

eligibility: Be a national of a World Bank member developing country on the published 2027 eligible list

Not be an Executive Director, his/her alternate, and/or staff of any type of appointment of the World Bank Group, and not be a close relative of any of the aforementioned by blood or adoption (close relative defined as Mother, Father, Sister, Half-sister, Brother, Half-brother, Son, Daughter, Aunt, Uncle, Niece, or Nephew)
Individuals who have previously been offered a JJ/WBGSP scholarship but declined it, or who previously received a JJ/WBGSP scholarship but did not graduate, are not eligible to apply again
Exception: applicants from a country on the list of Fragile and Conflict States in Annex 3 of the Application Guidelines may have their limited employment opportunities taken into consideration
requirements: Must already hold an unconditional admission letter (except for funding) from a JJ/WBGSP participating master's program, located outside the applicant's country of citizenship and country of residence as listed when the call opened
The letter of admission must be uploaded before submitting the scholarship application

All eligibility criteria are strictly adhered to with no exceptions; they will not change during an open call for applications
scholarships.duration: The duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less
scholarships.application_period: Two application rounds per cycle, organised to match the academic calendars of the participating programmes. For the 2027 cycle: Application Window #1 January 18 - February 26, 2027; Application Window #2 March 29 - May 21, 2027. Each participating university sets its own admission deadlines, which fall before the JJ/WBGSP window closes.
scholarships.selection_notes: Two qualified assessors independently review each eligible application and score it from 1 to 10 on four factors: quality of professional experience (30% weight), quality of professional recommendations (30% weight), quality of commitment to the applicant's home country (30% weight), and quality of education background (10% weight). The Secretariat uses the average of the two assessors plus a reasonably wide geographical distribution of awards, a reasonable distribution across gender, unusual circumstances or hardships, and giving scholarships to applicants who otherwise have limited access to financial resources for graduate studies abroad. Finalists go to the JJ/WBGSP Steering Committee, composed of members of the World Bank Board of Directors and World Bank management, for approval.
scholarships.name: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP) 2027 - Application Window #1 (Developing Country Nationals)
